# Where a contributor's description is lost

Section 1, recorded before anything was changed.

## No generated file carries a placeholder, and no body consumes one

```
grep -rc 'ARGUMENTS' .claude .codex .pi                     # 0 in every file
grep -rc 'ARGUMENTS' crates/htmlspec-assets/instructions/    # 0 in every body
```

Both halves are absent, and they are separate omissions. The frontmatter is what tells a
tool an argument exists; the body is what the tool substitutes into. A file with one and
not the other either declares an argument it ignores or consumes one no tool announced, so
the repair has to touch both.

## The two writers, and every field they emit

`write_skills` at `crates/htmlspec-cli/src/install.rs:88`:

```
name, description, allowed-tools, license, metadata.generatedBy
```

`write_commands` at `crates/htmlspec-cli/src/install.rs:124`:

```
description, allowed-tools, generatedBy
```

Listed in full so the omission is shown against a complete set rather than asserted.
Neither writes `argument-hint`. `write_region` at `:174` writes the `AGENTS.md` region and
has no invocation at all, so it is correctly absent from this list rather than a third
omission.

## The convention, from shipped artifacts rather than from memory

Claude Code's own example plugin, at
`~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-plugins-official/plugins/example-plugin/`:

`commands/example-command.md`
```
---
description: An example slash command that demonstrates command frontmatter options (legacy format)
argument-hint: <required-arg> [optional-arg]
allowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]
---
...
The user invoked this command with: $ARGUMENTS
```

`skills/example-command/SKILL.md` carries the same `argument-hint` and the same
`$ARGUMENTS`, and states: "It is functionally identical to the legacy
`commands/example-command.md` format — both are loaded the same way; only the file layout
differs."

That sentence is why both writers must change rather than only `write_commands`. This
program writes both kinds of file, and the two are loaded identically.

A Codex plugin command at `~/.codex/.tmp/plugins/plugins/vercel/commands/deploy.md`
branches on the substituted value:

```
If "$ARGUMENTS" contains "prod" or "production":
```

Two of the four tools with a command surface are confirmed to substitute. Cursor and Pi
are not confirmed by any artifact on this machine, which the design accepts as a stated
risk.

`plugin-dev`'s `command-development` skill documents the semantics: `$ARGUMENTS` captures
"all arguments as single string", so `/fix-issue 123` expands the token to `123`. One
placeholder for the whole remainder is all this change needs.

## No test asserts anything about arguments

```
grep -c 'argument-hint\|ARGUMENTS' crates/htmlspec-cli/src/install.rs   # 0
grep -c 'argument-hint\|ARGUMENTS' crates/htmlspec-cli/tests/cli.rs     # 0
```

The only occurrence of "argument" in `install.rs` is in its module comment, about the
functions being pure over their arguments. So the suite passing at 0.3.0 is expected rather
than evidence the invocation surface works: nothing looks at it. This is recorded first
because it is what makes the absence of a failing build unsurprising, and it is the same
shape of gap the previous change found in its own subject — a property no stage reads
stays wrong quietly.
